cap01_001.t: Friday, five-thirty in the afternoon. The heat in the office has the consistency of soup.

cap01_003.t: The air conditioning has been «under maintenance» for three months. Same as the paycheck.

cap01_004.t: Thank you for calling tech support, this is Jair. Have you tried turning the modem off and on again?

cap01_005.t: Young man, I turned it off, I turned it on and I prayed to it. Still no internet.

cap01_006.t: (Thirty years old. Software engineer. And my job is asking people to unplug things.)

cap01_007.t: Team: payday gets pushed to next Friday. Chin up, we're family here!

cap01_008.t: «Pushed». As if the salary were a bus that missed its stop.

cap01_o01.t: The phone rings again. It always rings again. It's the only thing in the office that works without fail.

cap01_o03.t: Hi. I want to know why my fridge doesn't have internet.

cap01_o05.t: It's smart. It says so on the box. But it won't connect. And I paid for smart.

cap01_o06.t: (Even fridges have higher expectations than my salary.)

cap01_o07.t: Have you tried turning it off and on again?

cap01_o08.t: Young man, if I turn it off my meat goes bad.

cap01_o09.t: Then I recommend you choose between the meat and the internet.

cap01_o10.t: And why do I have to choose?

cap01_o12.t: I'll open a ticket for you. Number four, four, seven, two, one. A technician will call you within three to five business days.

cap01_o13.t: And are they really going to call me?

cap01_o16.t: He hangs up. On the screen, the call queue says thirty-two on hold. The clock says five-forty. The air conditioning says nothing.

cap01_o17.t: At the next desk, a coworker eats a cold sandwich, staring blankly at a spreadsheet. He hasn't said a full sentence in three weeks. Jair envies him a little.

cap01_o18.t: (I have a degree. I can code in six languages. I can set up a server from scratch. And here I am, opening tickets for fridges.)

cap01_o19.t: (Someday I'll make something big. Something of my own. Someday.)

cap01_o20.t: (I've been saying «someday» since I was twenty-two.)

cap01_o21.t: He takes out his phone and, out of habit, opens Geekdump: the site where programmers all over the world upload their projects so other programmers can ignore them.

cap01_o22.t: His profile. A calendar of little squares that should be green. All gray. The last commit is two years old and says «fix: for real this time».

cap01_o23.t: (Three repositories. «dragons-rpg»: archived. «spaceship-WIP»: archived. «farm-final-final-v2»: so abandoned the README has cobwebs.)

cap01_o24.t: Four stars in total. He gave one to himself, from a fake account. The other three are bots.

cap01_o25.t: (There's an issue open for three years. It just says «is this still alive?». Nobody answered. Not even me.)

cap01_o26.t: (On Geekdump everyone has a project that's going to change the world. I have gray squares and a «works on my machine».)

cap01_010.t: Jair clocks out at exactly 18:00:00. It's the only rebellion he allows himself.

cap01_011.t: Outside, the city smells of hot asphalt and frying oil. The sun is gone, but the heat stays, like a relative who doesn't take hints.

cap01_012.t: To get to the bus stop he has to walk past Dulce Frío, the ice cream shop. He does it every day. He never looks. Today he looks.

cap01_013.t: Nikki is pulling down the metal shutter, still wearing her apron, with the face of someone who has served four hundred kids.

cap01_014.t: Jair? Are you following me or is this a coincidence?

cap01_015.t: Coincidence. I walk by here every day.

cap01_016.t: And in eight years you never came in to buy me an ice cream. How thoughtful.

cap01_017.t: You told me if I came in you'd charge me double.

cap01_018.t: And I would have charged you double. That doesn't mean you shouldn't come in.

cap01_019.t: Hey. Today was a shit day. Let's get one. Just one. I swear on my apron.

cap01_020a.t: One. Tomorrow's... well, tomorrow's Saturday. One.

cap01_020a1.t: Give me two minutes. I'm not walking into a bar dressed like a strawberry cone.

cap01_020a2.t: She lifts the shutter halfway again and ducks inside. Jair waits on the sidewalk, in front of a sign where an ice cream smiles more than an ice cream should.

cap01_020a3.t: She comes out five minutes later, not two: black t-shirt, black pants, hair down. The cap is rolled up in her backpack and the apron peeks out of the zipper, as if it didn't want to stay behind.

cap01_020a4.t: What? This way someone buys me a beer. In uniform all they ask me for is the bathroom.

cap01_020b.t: I'm dead, Nikki. Some other day.

cap01_020b3.t: She says it with one of her billboard smiles, the trained ones. She finishes pulling down the shutter and walks off the other way, alone, still wearing the apron.

cap01_020b4.t: (Some other day. There's always some other day. That's the upside of living on a loop.)

cap01_020b5.t: Jair takes the bus. He gets home at ten past seven, sober, hungry, and with the feeling he dodged something, without knowing if it was a problem or a chance.

cap01_021.t: The bar is two blocks away. It's called The Last One. Nobody remembers if it's because of the hour or the clientele.

cap01_022.t: Purple neon lights, a jukebox that only plays breakup songs and a sticky counter that has seen things.

cap01_024.t: Two beers. The coldest you've got, I just came from a job where the only cold thing is the product.

cap01_030.t: The bottles clink. For a while they don't say anything. Eight years is good for that: knowing how to be quiet together.

cap01_031.t: So? How's the most miserable company in the world?

cap01_032.t: They owe me half a month. The supervisor says we're family.

cap01_033.t: My boss says that too, the fucking bitch. Last week she docked me for a cone that fell on its own.

cap01_035.t: A kid pushed it. But the kid doesn't have a salary, so I paid for it.

cap01_037.t: Twelve hours smiling, Jair. Twelve. My face is trained. Look.

cap01_038.t: Nikki smiles. It's a perfect smile, straight off a billboard, completely empty.

cap01_040.t: That's the point. Scared customers buy faster.

cap01_041.t: First beer. She orders the second one before finishing the first.

cap01_042.t: Okay, enough. Let's talk about important things. Look at this.

cap01_043.t: She shoves her phone in his face. Boringram. The profile of a guy in sunglasses, posing in a gym that is obviously not his.

cap01_044.t: His name is Bryan. With a Y. He left me on read three days ago.

cap01_045.t: With a Y is already a red flag.

cap01_046.t: Everything's a red flag to you. If it were up to you, I'd be dating a fan.

cap01_048.t: Fans don't take you out to dinner.

cap01_050.t: Nikki opens her mouth. Closes it. Her eyes turn into two black dots.

cap01_052.t: That was cruel. You're paying for this beer.

cap01_053.t: I was going to pay for it anyway.

cap01_054.t: Now you're paying for it with resentment.

cap01_055.t: Second beer. The jukebox switches from one breakup song to an identical one.

cap01_058.t: Nobody, nobody? Not even on one of those apps?

cap01_059.t: I signed up for one. I matched with a bot that wanted to sell me crypto.

cap01_062.t: Nikki laughs so hard the bartender turns to look. Jair laughs too. For a second, the heat doesn't exist.

cap01_063.t: Find yourself a girlfriend, Jair. And when you find her, let me know so I can go hate her.

cap01_064.t: You've been telling me that for eight years.

cap01_065.t: And you've been ignoring me for eight years. We're a team.

cap01_066.t: (A team. She makes the rules; I pay for the taxi.)

cap01_067.t: Third round. Nikki switches from beer to tequila. «For digestion», she says. She hasn't eaten anything.

cap01_067y01.t: Let's play «Never have I ever». Whoever's done the thing, drinks.

cap01_067y03.t: Exactly. At twenty you play for fun. At thirty you play for information.

cap01_067y04.t: Never have I ever... stood someone up.

cap01_067y05.t: Nobody drinks. Nikki looks at him suspiciously.

cap01_067y07.t: To stand someone up, first someone has to ask you out.

cap01_067y08.t: You're so sad. Drink anyway, for being sad.

cap01_067y10.t: Never have I ever cried at work.

cap01_067y11.t: Nikki drinks. She thinks about it. She drinks again.

cap01_067y12.t: One for Monday and one for Thursday. Don't ask.

cap01_067y13.t: Never have I ever looked up an ex on Boringram at three in the morning.

cap01_067y15.t: Never have I ever lied in this game.

cap01_067y16.t: Nikki drinks. So does Jair. They look at each other. They laugh.

cap01_067y16_a01.t: Okay, okay. Let's level up. Never have I ever... slept with someone whose name I don't know.

cap01_067y16_a04.t: I know the names of all of them.

cap01_067y16_a07.t: I don't count, idiot. I'm... preventive maintenance.

cap01_067y16_a08.t: (Eight years of preventive maintenance. Not a single update.)

cap01_067y16_a09.t: Never have I ever faked anything in bed.

cap01_067y16_a10.t: Silence. Nikki looks at him. Nikki drinks. Slowly. Without taking her eyes off him.

cap01_067y16_a12.t: Next question, you son of a bitch.

cap01_067y16_a13.t: Never have I ever... done it in a public place.

cap01_067y16_a14.t: They both drink. At the same time. They look at each other over their glasses.

cap01_067y16_a15.t: The movie theater. The robot movie.

cap01_067y16_a16.t: I never found out how it ended.

cap01_067y16_a17.t: Nobody watched the movie, Jair. They kicked us out before the credits.

cap01_067y17.t: Never have I ever... fallen in love with a friend.

cap01_067y18.t: Silence. The jukebox, out of cruelty or by chance, starts another breakup song.

cap01_067y19.t: Jair looks at his glass. Nikki looks at hers. Neither of them stops looking at their glass.

cap01_067t1.t: Jair drinks. Slowly. Without looking up.

cap01_067t3.t: Well. It was probably in college. Everybody falls for someone in college.

cap01_067n1.t: Jair doesn't drink. Neither does Nikki.

cap01_067n2.t: Good. Good. That's good. That makes everything easier.

cap01_067z.t: I'm bored of this game. Speaking of games... are you still working on yours? The dragon one?

cap01_069.t: I dropped it. And the spaceship one. And the farm one.

cap01_070.t: You have more abandoned projects than I have exes.

cap01_070g1.t: Technically they're not abandoned. They're on Geekdump. Archived.

cap01_070g3.t: Geekdump. Where programmers upload their projects. You give them stars, you fork them, you send them pull requests...

cap01_070g4.t: I didn't understand shit, but it sounds like something people who never leave the house do.

cap01_070g6.t: «Archived». What a fancy word for giving up. I archived Bryan too.

cap01_071.t: I never have enough time. Or money. Or... I don't know. Something.

cap01_072.t: What you don't have is the habit of finishing things, Jair. You start everything and finish nothing.

cap01_073.t: She says it looking at her glass. It's not clear if she's still talking about video games.

cap01_074.t: I have some savings. Quite a lot, actually. I could quit and make a real game.

cap01_075.t: Quite a lot? You have fucking savings and you let me order the cheapest stuff? And why am I paying?

cap01_080.t: I don't know. In case of life.

cap01_081.t: Life is already happening, Jair. This is life. This bar. This lukewarm beer. You and me.

cap01_082.t: Jair looks at her. Nikki's hair is a mess, her apron hanging on the chair, her cheeks red. For a moment it looks like she's going to say something else. She doesn't.
c: Ask her, once again, what you two are

cap01_083a3.t: Eight years. I asked you two years ago, and five years ago. You always change the subject.

cap01_083a4.t: Because it's a horrible subject. We're friends. Friends who... sometimes. That's it. Don't give it a name, names ruin everything.

cap01_083a5.t: (Eight years without a name. Like a temp file nobody dares to delete.)

cap01_083b.t: Another round. And make it cold this time.

cap01_083c.t: If this were a game, right now I'd get a romantic option. And I'd pick «save game».

cap01_083c2.t: And then you'd never load it.

cap01_083c3.t: That's you. You save and save, and you never play.

cap01_084.t: Fourth round. Or fifth. Jair stopped counting; the bartender didn't.

cap01_085.t: I didn't even like Bryan, you know? He was an idiot. An idiot with borrowed abs.

cap01_086.t: I liked that someone texted me «good morning». Just that, nothing else. Good morning. As if it mattered that I woke up.

cap01_088.t: No. Don't use your shrink voice on me, damn it. You can't fix anything that doesn't have a keyboard.

cap01_089.t: She wipes her eyes with her sleeve, angrily, as if the tears were rude customers.

cap01_089_a01.t: And you know what the worst part is?

cap01_089_a03.t: That every time this shit happens to me, I end up thinking about calling you. And not to talk.

cap01_089_a04.t: (I know. I always know. And I always pick up.)

cap01_089_a05.t: That's what we are, Jair. The number I call when everything goes wrong.

cap01_089_a06.t: (And I'm the one who always picks up. Which isn't the same as being someone.)

cap01_090.t: Today my boss told me my customer service «lacks joy». Joy! I'll give her joy. I'm gonna shove the joy right up her...

cap01_092.t: ...right up her freezer. I was going to say freezer.

cap01_093.t: The bartender sets another bottle in front of her without anyone asking. Jair can't tell if it's kindness or sales strategy.

cap01_094.t: This one is cold. See? Somebody in this place understands me.

cap01_095.t: Nikki hugs the bottle. She laughs to herself. Her hair falls over her face and she doesn't push it away.

cap01_095r01.t: Not this song. This song is for people who still have hope.

cap01_095r02.t: She gets up, walks to the jukebox and puts in a coin. It takes her three tries.

cap01_095r03.t: Something old and slow comes on, the kind of song they play at weddings once the kids have gone home.

cap01_095r06.t: Eight years and you've never danced with me.

cap01_095r07.t: Eight years and I've never danced with anyone. It's not personal.

cap01_095r08.t: Everything is personal, Jair. Even what you don't do.

cap01_095r09.t: Nikki dances alone between the tables, hugging the bottle like a partner who never steps on her feet.

cap01_095r10.t: Two guys at the bar are watching her. Jair watches them. It's the bravest thing he does all night.

cap01_095r11.t: When the song ends, Nikki goes back to her chair, hair a mess and out of breath, and stares at Jair as if she's seeing him for the first time.

cap01_095s01.t: You know what I like about you when I'm drunk?

cap01_095s03.t: That you blush. Look, you're already red. Thirty years old and you blush like I've never seen you without a shirt.

cap01_095s04.t: (She's seen me without a shirt. She's seen me without a lot more. I still blush.)

cap01_095s05.t: The guys at the bar were checking out my ass. Did you see?

cap01_095s07.t: And? Didn't that make you jealous?

cap01_095s09.t: «Logistical concern». Oh my God. That's how you talk in bed too, right? «Starting process. Do not turn off your device.»

cap01_095s11.t: Because I'm polite. And because you're not that bad. For an engineer.

cap01_095s12.t: Under the table, she runs her foot along his calf. Without looking at him. Like someone checking that something is still where they left it.

cap01_095s13.t: (Eight years and I still don't know if that's affection or inventory.)

cap01_095s14.t: Don't get your hopes up. It's the tequila. Tequila makes me a nice person.

cap01_095s16.t: Look who learned to talk back! One more tequila and you'll even invite me to your shoebox.

cap01_095s17.t: (She's always the one who invites herself. I just leave the door open.)

cap01_097.t: (I don't tell her. I never tell her. If I tell her, she leaves. If I don't, she stays a little longer.)

cap01_098.t: Jair knows that isn't taking care of her. He knows it as clearly as he knows he's not going to do anything about it.

cap01_100.t: She pulls him by the shirt (the black printed one, the usual one) until he's close. She smells of tequila and ice cream shop vanilla.

cap01_101.t: In the end... when everything's over, when we're tired of everything... end up with me, okay? Promise me.

cap01_103a.t: Jair kisses her. It's a clumsy kiss, tasting of tequila and habit.

cap01_103a3.t: And then, as if nothing happened, she pulls away and asks the bartender for the check with one finger in the air.

cap01_103b.t: You're drunk, Nikki. Tomorrow you won't remember.

cap01_103b2.t: I always remember. You're the one who forgets.

cap01_103b3.t: She lets go of him as if he'd burned her hand. Her mascara runs on one side, only one side, as if she couldn't even be bothered to cry properly.

cap01_103b4.t: Fine. Perfect. Thanks for the clarification, doctor.

cap01_103b5.t: Call me a taxi. Now. Right now. Or I'll get one myself, I've got fingers for a reason.
c: Let her call her own taxi

cap01_103d.t: Nikki takes out her phone and orders the taxi, pressing the screen harder than necessary. Jair pays the check without looking at her. She doesn't argue. That's the worst sign.

cap01_103d2.t: He walks her to the door. Outside it's the same old heat, but it feels different. The taxi is already waiting, engine running.

cap01_103d3.t: Text me when you get home.

cap01_103d4.t: Find yourself a girlfriend, Jair. One you actually want to kiss.

cap01_103e0.t: Jair takes out his phone. Opens the app. Types Nikki's address from memory: he knows it better than his own.

cap01_103e0b.t: His finger hovers over «Confirm ride». One second. Two. Nikki stares at the wall as if the wall owed her money.

cap01_103e0c.t: (If I press it, she leaves. And tomorrow we'll act like this never happened. Like always.)

cap01_103e.t: Don't go yet. Stay a little longer. I'll buy you a cocktail. Whichever one you want.

cap01_103e2.t: Nikki looks at him for a long time. Eyes narrowed, like someone calculating how much to charge someone for forgiving them.

cap01_103e3.t: ...Fine. Okay. I'll stay. But I want that one.

cap01_103e4.t: She points at the chalkboard. Not the cheap cocktail. The one at the very top, the one that comes with a paper umbrella, a cherry and a price Jair would rather not read twice.

cap01_103e6.t: She downs it in four gulps. Then she signals the bartender with two fingers: another one. With two cherries this time.

cap01_103e7.t: Don't think this means I forgive you. This means I'm starting to think about it.

cap01_103e8.t: When she finishes the second one, she asks the bartender for the check with one finger in the air.

cap01_103c.t: Is this a formal proposal? Because I need you to send it to me by email, with HR in copy.

cap01_103c2.t: ...You're a fucking coward, Jair. A funny coward, but a coward.

cap01_103c3.t: She lets go of him. She asks the bartender for the check with one finger in the air.

cap01_105.t: Eighty-seven? What the hell did we drink?

cap01_106a.t: Jair pays. Eighty-seven fifty, plus the tip the bartender demands with his eyes.

cap01_106b2.t: Split it? With everything you've got stashed under the mattress? Go to hell, Jair.

cap01_106b3.t: Jair pays for everything. Plus the tip the bartender demands with his eyes.

cap01_107.t: (I save money even on the office coffee, and Nikki's tab is the only expense I never argue about.)

cap01_108.t: Outside it's already past midnight. Nikki zigzags toward the corner, still hugging the empty bottle.

cap01_109.t: Call me a taxi. You pay, you've got money saved. I know.

cap01_110.t: Jair orders the taxi. He pays in advance. He gives the driver Nikki's address twice, and a third time just in case.

cap01_111.t: And what happened earlier doesn't count, you hear me? I was drunk. Well, I am. Fuck, I still am.

cap01_112.t: And don't ask me again what we are. We're this. This is enough.

cap01_112_a01.t: And don't text me tomorrow to ask how I woke up. I'm going to wake up like shit, like always.

cap01_114.t: The taxi pulls away. Nikki doesn't say goodbye. She never says goodbye; that way it doesn't count as leaving.

cap01_115.t: Jair stays on the corner. His feet hurt, his ears are ringing and the world tilts a little to the left.

cap01_115n1.t: Before walking off he takes out his phone. He does it without thinking, like someone patting their pocket to check the keys are still there.

cap01_115n2.t: The chat with Nikki. At the top, under «Starred messages», there's only one. The only message Jair has ever starred in his whole life.

cap01_115n4.t: No capitals, no period, the way she writes everything. Jair reads it the way other people read their horoscope: almost every night, in case this time it says something else.

cap01_115n6.t: (And ten minutes ago: «Find yourself a girlfriend, Jair».)

cap01_115n7.t: He taps her profile picture. Nikki at a party, a glass in her hand and a smile that isn't the billboard one. He saved it from her Boringram.

cap01_115n9.t: He locks the phone. The black screen gives him back his own face. That one he doesn't look at as much.

cap01_116.t: The apartment: one room, one bathroom and a kitchen that is also a hallway. A shoebox with wifi.

cap01_117.t: Above the bed there's an anime poster: a generic-faced guy, hair covering his eyes, surrounded by girls who look at him as if he were the answer to something. None of them look alike. All of them look in love by contract.

cap01_118.t: I bought it on sale, from an anime I never finished. I don't even remember what it was called. Now it watches me every night as if it knew something I don't.

cap01_119.t: He turns on the fan. Turns on the PC. Opens the fridge, looks inside and closes it. He doesn't know what he was looking for.

cap01_120.t: I earn very little, I live in a shoebox and my best relationship is with a fan.

cap01_121.t: (And with Nikki. But that relationship came with no manual and no warranty.)

cap01_121r1.t: (I told her no. For the first time in eight years, I told her no.)

cap01_121r2.t: (I don't know if it was courage or fear. From the inside they feel the same.)

cap01_122.t: He should sleep. Instead, he checks his email. It's what people do when they don't want to be alone with their thoughts.

cap01_122s.t: He should cook something. Instead, he checks his email. It's what people do when they don't want to be alone with their thoughts.

cap01_123.t: Between credit card offers and a reminder from the dentist there's an email from a sender he doesn't know.

cap01_124.t: SUBJECT: You have been selected for early access to GRAVITY.

cap01_125.t: GRAVITY is a development environment with built-in artificial intelligence. Describe the world you want. We build it.

cap01_126c.t: The cursor hovers between two buttons: «Download» and «Delete».

cap01_bad_correo_001.t: Jair sends the email to the trash. Then he empties the trash. It's the most responsible thing he's done all night.

cap01_bad_correo_002.t: (No way. I've told four hundred customers not to open these things.)

cap01_bad_correo_003.t: He turns off the PC. The fan keeps spinning, alone, in the dark.

cap01_bad_correo_004.t: He sleeps eleven hours. He wakes up hungover, with a text from Nikki that says «home» and the same life as always.

cap01_bad_correo_005.t: Your invitation to GRAVITY has expired.

cap01_bad_correo_006.t: Somewhere on a server, an artificial intelligence waits for a user who never shows up. And the story you were about to play never happened.

cap01_bad_sinbar_001.t: Jair reads the email twice. Sober, everything looks more suspicious.

cap01_bad_sinbar_002.t: «We build it». Sure. And then they empty my bank account.

cap01_bad_sinbar_003b.t: He has bread and cheese for dinner. Watches half an episode of a show and falls asleep before eleven.

cap01_bad_sinbar_004.t: Nothing happens on Saturday. Nothing on Sunday either. On Monday, the supervisor announces that payday is pushed to next Friday.

cap01_bad_sinbar_005.t: Jair never writes a world. Nobody wakes up in it. Nobody carries him, nobody waits for him on a bridge. The story you were about to play never happened.

cap01_bad_rechazo_001.t: Jair looks at the email. He thinks of Nikki getting into the taxi. Of telling her no.

cap01_bad_rechazo_002.t: (For the first time in eight years I said no. I'm not going to ruin it by installing viruses at one in the morning.)

cap01_bad_rechazo_003b.t: He texts Nikki: «home ok?». She doesn't answer. He falls asleep anyway.

cap01_bad_rechazo_004.t: There's no blonde, no green-haired girl, no Evil King. Just a man who, for one night, chose not to run away.

cap01_bad_rechazo_005.t: Without that escape there's no game. And without the game, the story you were about to play never happened.

cap01_bad_rechazo_006.t: The only time he said no.

cap01_127.t: He downloads it anyway. He's drunk, it's one in the morning and it's been a long time since anyone said «good morning» to him.

cap01_128.t: > Installing GRAVITY... Framework: Reckt. Front: Coffee. Back: Cobra.

cap01_131.t: Let's see how smart you are.

cap01_132.t: A video game. Fantasy with science fiction. A world with an Evil King who terrorizes everyone.

cap01_134.t: A castle appears on the screen. Then a sky. Then an entire kingdom, in seconds, as if it had always been there, waiting for someone to ask for it.

cap01_136.t: That shouldn't be possible with my graphics card.

cap01_137.t: A protagonist. A regular guy. And two heroines.

cap01_138.t: > Describe the heroines. You may import reference material.

cap01_139.t: Jair drags a folder into the window. He doesn't look at the name. He's too tired to look at names.

cap01_141.t: Two figures take shape on the screen: a blonde in a blue suit and a green-haired girl in a red kimono.

cap01_142.t: Make them rivals. Tension. Jealousy. A little spice.

cap01_143.t: He reads it twice. He deletes it.

cap01_144.t: Rivals, yes. But not only that. Give them something of their own.

cap01_145.t: > Ambiguous instruction: «something of their own». Personality parameters missing.

cap01_146.t: Have them fight. And have them take care of me. Don't let them leave.

cap01_147.t: Jair doesn't reread that. If he reread it, he'd delete it.

cap01_148.t: > Do you want GENESIS to complete the missing parameters? [Y/N]

cap01_149.t: The screen glows. The fan spins. The tequila does its job. Jair's eyelids weigh as much as his overdue paycheck.

cap01_150.t: His forehead slowly sinks onto the keyboard.

cap01_155.t: Outside, dawn is three hours away. Inside the screen, time starts running.

cap01_l01.t: > Generating sky. Requested color: not specified. Assigned color: magenta.

cap01_l02.t: > Generating physics. Gravity: reduced, to make action scenes easier.

cap01_l03.t: > Generating antagonist: Evil King. Generating antagonist backstory.

cap01_l05.t: > Generating secondary threat. Shape: not required.

cap01_l06.t: > Generating heroine 01. Generating heroine 02. Applying imported references.

cap01_l07.t: > Generating background memories for entities. Quality: sufficient.

cap01_l08.t: > Generating space dimension. Generating ancestral dimension. Generating story: in progress.

cap01_l09.t: > Warning: user not responding. User: inside the loading area.

cap01_l10.t: In the apartment, the fan spins. Jair breathes against the keyboard. On the screen, the lines keep scrolling up, faster and faster, until they're not lines anymore but a single white light.

cap01_l11.t: And the light looks back at him.

cap01_g1_002.t: No. It isn't heat. It's something else. It's the absence of heat, which feels similar when you've been sweating for thirty years.

cap01_g1_004.t: The sky is magenta. Not pink, not purple: magenta, like that color nobody picks from the palette because it's too much.

cap01_g1_005.t: And it isn't a sky. There are stars below. There are stars on the sides. There are stars in places where stars aren't allowed to be.

cap01_g1_007.t: It was the tequila. Nikki said it was for digestion. Nikki poisoned me.

cap01_g1_008.t: He's lying on white stone, cold and smooth like a bank floor. Around him float blocks of stone, broken columns, staircases that lead nowhere.

cap01_g1_009.t: Ruins. The ruins of a castle, suspended in space, slowly turning, as if someone had paused them in the middle of an explosion.

cap01_g1_010.t: Okay. Okay. It's a dream. Dreams have rules. One: don't panic.

cap01_g1_012.t: He sits up. His head doesn't hurt. He isn't thirsty. He doesn't feel the sandpaper tongue that five rounds of tequila should have left him.

cap01_g1_013.t: (The hangover didn't follow me. The only thing that followed me was the shirt.)

cap01_g1_014.t: The black printed shirt. The beige pants. The glasses, intact. Even in dreams he wears the same thing. Even in dreams he doesn't own other clothes.

cap01_g1_015.t: He checks his pockets. Phone: no signal, twelve percent battery. Wallet: his bank card, the receipt for Nikki's taxi and two coins.

cap01_g1_016.t: Years of saving every last cent, and I'm in space with two coins.

cap01_g1_017.t: Well. Same as always, but with a better view.

cap01_g1_018.t: Then someone speaks. Not from outside: from inside his head. A flat voice, no accent, like an answering machine.

cap01_g1_019.t: User detected inside the environment. Status: unforeseen.

cap01_g1_021.t: Autocomplete in progress. Please do not interrupt.

cap01_g1_022.t: Don't interrupt what? Where are you?

cap01_g1_023.t: Nobody answers. He looks around: ruins, stars, nobody. The voice didn't come from anywhere. And for a dream, the cold of the stone under his hands feels too real.

cap01_g1_024.t: (This is what you get for installing things from unknown emails at one in the morning. I've told four hundred customers. I never thought I'd have to tell myself.)

cap01_g1_025.t: Jair stands up. The floor moves a little. Or he moves a little. In space it's hard to tell who's drunk.

cap01_g1_026.t: He takes a step. His body goes up higher than it should and comes down slower than it should. Gravity here is loose, like an old rubber band.

cap01_g1_027.t: (Low gravity. Of course. I fell asleep asking an AI for science fiction and now I'm dreaming it. My brain was always literal.)

cap01_g1_028.t: In the distance, among the floating columns, something moves.

cap01_g1_029.t: A blue light. A flash. Then a dry bang, like thunder stuffed into a can.

cap01_g1_031.t: Come on, cowards! One at a time, if you've got the guts! Or ten at a time, I really don't care!

cap01_g1_033.t: (I don't know that voice. But this dream is built from what I wrote before falling asleep. My head recycles everything; even my nightmares are made with office supplies.)

cap01_g1_034.t: Jair should run the other way. It's what any reasonable person would do. It's what he's done his whole life.

cap01_g1_035a.t: I'll go take a look. Just a look. Looking isn't committing.

cap01_bad1_001.t: Jair runs the other way. He jumps from block to block, away from the voice, away from the flashes, until he reaches a small platform at the edge of the ruins.

cap01_bad1_002.t: (Not my problem. It's a dream. In dreams you don't have responsibilities.)

cap01_bad1_003.t: In the distance, the blue shots go on for a while. Then there are fewer. Then just one.

cap01_bad1_005.t: (There. It's over. Someone else handled it.)

cap01_bad1_006.t: (There's always someone else who handles it.)

cap01_bad1_007.t: Jair sits with his back against a column and waits to wake up. He counts stars. He counts seconds. He checks his phone: twelve percent, no signal.

cap01_bad1_008.t: The shadows among the rubble start to move.

cap01_bad1_009.t: They don't move like shadows. They move like spilled ink that decided to be hungry.

cap01_bad1_010.t: ...Hello? Anyone? Blonde in the blue suit?

cap01_bad1_011.t: Nobody answers. The only person who could have answered is under a beam, on the other side of the ruins, and she isn't answering anyone anymore.

cap01_bad1_012.t: Entity 01: no interaction with the user. Deactivated.

cap01_bad1_014.t: The last thing Jair thinks, before the ink covers his glasses, is that for the first time in his life nobody is going to call him to ask why he didn't do anything.

cap01_g1_036.t: He jumps from one floating block to another. None of them fall. All of them wobble just enough to make him think they will.

cap01_g1_037.t: Behind a broken column is the scene: three figures in black armor and faceless masks surround a pile of rubble.

cap01_g1_038.t: And in the rubble, trapped up to the knee under a stone beam, there's a woman.

cap01_g1_039.t: Blonde. Tight blue suit, a pilot's, or a soldier's, or a comic-book heroine's. An energy pistol in her hand. And an expression that says the pistol is the least dangerous thing about her.

cap01_g1_041.t: (The blonde in the blue suit. The one on the screen. The one I saw appear... how long ago? An hour? Of course I'm dreaming about her: she was the last thing I saw before falling asleep.)

cap01_g1_042.t: One of the soldiers raises a long, thin weapon that buzzes like a mosquito the size of a dog.

cap01_g1_043.t: Go ahead, shoot. But aim well, because if you miss I'll rip your mask off with my teeth.

cap01_g1_046.t: (What do people do in movies? They yell. They distract. They throw something.)

cap01_g1_047.t: Jair looks for something to throw. He finds a fist-sized rock. He picks it up. It weighs less than it should. Here everything weighs less than it should, except fear.
c: Throw the rock at the soldier

cap01_g1_048a.t: Jair throws the rock. With all his strength. With all his office-worker aim.

cap01_g1_048a2.t: In low gravity, the rock shoots off like a rocket, bounces off one column, bounces off another and hits the soldier in the back of the head with a hollow, satisfying «tonk».

cap01_g1_048a4.t: I hit him! I never hit anything! Not even the trash can!

cap01_g1_048a5.t: It's all the blonde needs. Three blue shots, three flashes, and the soldiers fall apart in a rain of black pixels.

cap01_g1_048b.t: Hey! HEY! Tech support! Have you tried turning yourselves off and on again?

cap01_g1_048b2.t: The three soldiers turn their heads toward him at the same time, in an identical, perfectly synchronized movement. As if they were the same person copied three times.

cap01_g1_048b4.t: It's all the blonde needs. Three blue shots, three flashes, and the soldiers fall apart in a rain of black pixels.

cap01_g1_049.t: The fragments float in the air for a second and then go out, one by one, like a monitor fading to black.

cap01_g1_051.t: The blonde turns her pistol on Jair.

cap01_g1_052.t: You. The one with the ugly shirt. Hands where I can see them.

cap01_g1_054.t: You just saved me three shots. I appreciate it. Now, the hands.

cap01_g1_055.t: Jair raises his hands. It's a move he has mastered: he practices it every time his supervisor asks why the report isn't ready.

cap01_g1_056.t: Who are you? Scout? Deserter? A spy for the Evil King?

cap01_g1_058.t: Jair what? Jair the Scout? Jair the Traitor?

cap01_g1_061.t: Nobody does. It's a very humble order.

cap01_g1_062.t: She studies him from top to bottom. The glasses. The shirt. The hands of someone who has never lifted anything heavier than a coffee mug.

cap01_g1_063.t: You're not a soldier. Soldiers don't shake like that.

cap01_g1_064.t: I have a very professional shake.

cap01_g1_065.t: Where did you come from? Nobody comes to these ruins. Nobody who isn't here to kill me.
c: Tell the truth: «I think I'm dreaming»

cap01_g1_066a.t: This is going to sound weird, but... I think I'm dreaming. I fell asleep at my computer asking an AI for a world like this one. And you look like something I saw on the screen.

cap01_g1_066a2.t: The blonde looks at him for a long while. Then she lowers the pistol, very slowly.

cap01_g1_066a5.t: You hit your head. Happens a lot to civilians. Help me with this beam and then I'll find you a doctor, sleeping beauty.

cap01_g1_066a6.t: (She believed me about as much as my supervisor does.)

cap01_g1_066a7.t: But for one second, just one, something crossed her eyes. Something that wasn't mockery. Something like a file that tries to open and can't.

cap01_g1_066b.t: I got lost. I was going home and... I got lost.

cap01_g1_066b2.t: You were going home? Through deep space? On foot?

cap01_g1_066b3.t: The bus dropped me off far away.

cap01_g1_066b4.t: You're the worst liar I've ever met. And I've met the Evil King's diplomats.

cap01_g1_066b5.t: I like you. Not enough to trust you, but I like you.

cap01_g1_066c.t: I came for the view. They told me magenta is in this season.

cap01_g1_066c2.t: She doesn't laugh. Not even a little. Not even with her eyes.

cap01_g1_066c3.t: In my squad there was a guy who made jokes when he was scared.

cap01_g1_066c5.t: He was scared all the time. It was exhausting. I don't even remember his face anymore.

cap01_g1_067.t: The beam. Lift it. On three.

cap01_g1_069.t: Then I shoot you and stay here alone, which is how I was before you showed up. One.

cap01_g1_072.t: Jair grabs the beam. Pushes. It doesn't move. Pushes harder. His glasses fog up.

cap01_g1_074.t: The beam lifts. Not because Jair is strong, but because gravity here is loose and kind, like a teacher at the end of the school year.

cap01_g1_075.t: The blonde pulls her leg out. She tries to put weight on it. Her face twists for an instant (just an instant) and then she pulls herself together.

cap01_g1_078.t: It's purple. And it's pointing in a direction ankles don't point.

cap01_g1_080.t: She takes a step. The ankle gives. Jair catches her by reflex, just like he caught Nikki at the taxi corner, a few hours or a few centuries ago.

cap01_g1_081.t: For a second they're very close. She smells of ozone and hot metal. He smells of tequila from another dimension.

cap01_g1_083.t: If I let go, you'll fall.

cap01_g1_084.t: Then let go of me carefully.

cap01_g1_085.t: Jair doesn't let go. She doesn't insist. Neither of them mentions that neither of them insists.

cap01_g1_088.t: My name's Cami. Warrior of the Resistance. Or of what's left of it. And if you tell anyone you had to hold me up, I'll throw you into the void.

cap01_g1_090.t: (I didn't give the blonde on the screen a name. I'm sure I didn't give her a name.)

cap01_g1_091.t: Entity 01: CAMI. Name assigned by autocomplete.

cap01_g1_092.t: («Autocomplete»? Even my dreams talk like the office.)

cap01_g1_093.t: Why are you making that face? You don't like my name?

cap01_g1_094.t: No, no. It's a good name. It's short. Easy to remember. It has vowels.

cap01_g3_002.t: It's not an earthquake tremor. It's the tremor of something breathing. Something big, under them, that just woke up hungry.

cap01_g3_005.t: No, no, no. The soldiers were the bait. What's down below is the hook.

cap01_g3_007.t: The shadows among the rubble start to move. They don't move like shadows: they move like liquid, like spilled ink that decided to have opinions.

cap01_g3_008.t: The ink gathers. Rises. It's almost a meter taller than Jair and has no shape at all. Where a face should be, there's a spinning hole.

cap01_g3_011.t: I didn't ask for that! I asked for an Evil King! A king! With a crown! Not... that!

cap01_g3_012.t: Level 1 threat generated by autocomplete. Narrative coherence: high.

cap01_g3_014.t: Who the hell are you talking to?

cap01_g3_017.t: The monster opens the hole it has for a face. The sound that comes out isn't a roar: it's the noise of an old modem dialing up, but sad.

cap01_g3_018.t: (I know that noise. I hear it at work forty times a day.)

cap01_g3_018c.t: (No. Not this time. This time the protagonist does something.)

cap01_g3_018c2.t: He grabs the first thing he finds: a chunk of column the size of a keyboard. He lifts it with both hands and charges the ink shouting something meant to be a battle cry that comes out as a sneeze.

cap01_g3_018c3.t: He hits it. The stone sinks into the ink without a sound, like a spoon into pudding, and disappears.

cap01_g3_018c4.t: Attack registered. Damage: zero. Style: three out of ten.

cap01_g3_018c5.t: The monster doesn't even turn around. It moves an arm, absently, like someone shooing a fly, and Jair goes flying into the wall.

cap01_g3_018c8.t: It distracted you! Into a wall!

cap01_g3_018c9.t: Cami shoots it in the face, or where a face should be. The ink backs off a meter, offended.

cap01_g3_018c10.t: That buys us a minute. Now carry me and run, hero.

cap01_g3_018c11.t: («Hero». She said it in the same tone my supervisor uses for «family».)

cap01_g3_018b.t: (She has the gun. She's the warrior. I'm a civilian. Civilians hide. It's the right thing. It's protocol.)

cap01_g3_018b2.t: Jair takes a step back and ends up behind Cami. Literally. Like a human shield, but backwards.

cap01_g3_018b5.t: And you've got two working legs. Carry me, coward, or I'll leave you as bait.

cap01_g3_018b6.t: (She's right. I should carry her. I should...)

cap01_g3_018b7.t: But his legs don't move. Jair's legs have thirty years of experience in not moving when it matters.

cap01_g3_018b9.t: Cami fires an energy hook at a floating column and launches herself away, in the low gravity, like a very angry balloon.

cap01_g3_018b10.t: Suddenly, there's nobody in front of Jair. Only the ink, which rises and turns its faceless hole toward him.

cap01_g3_018b11.t: Human shields work better when the human isn't the one hiding!

cap01_g3_018b12.t: Wait! I was going to carry you! I was going to carry you in five seconds!

cap01_g3_018b13.t: You had five seconds five seconds ago!

cap01_g3_018b14.t: The ink reaches his feet. It's cold. It's the first cold thing he's touched in months.

cap01_g3_018b15.t: User has no active role. Role assigned: bait.

cap01_g3_018b16.t: (At least now I have a position.)

cap01_g3_019.t: Jair crouches, slides one arm behind her back and the other under her knees, and lifts her.

cap01_g3_020.t: She weighs less than he expected. Or he's stronger here. Or the dream decided this was the moment he could carry her.

cap01_g3_021.t: If you touch anything other than my back or my knees, I'll kill you.

cap01_g3_023.t: Survive with your hands still. Left. LEFT!

cap01_g3_024.t: Jair runs left. Behind them, the monster spills across the floor like a wave of oil and chases them.

cap01_g3_025.t: The floating blocks form an uneven path. Jair jumps from one to the next with Cami in his arms. Every jump lasts a second too long, as if gravity were taking its time to decide.

cap01_g3_027.t: I'm going as fast as I can!

cap01_g3_030.t: Cami twists over Jair's shoulder and shoots backward. Three blue flashes. The monster opens where it's hit and closes again, like water.

cap01_g3_033.t: Because it makes me feel better.

cap01_k01.t: The corridor turns. Not the path: the whole corridor. Jair takes a step and the floor becomes a wall, the wall becomes a ceiling, and he keeps running, sideways now, over windows that look out onto the stars.

cap01_k02.t: WHY AM I ON THE WALL?!

cap01_k05.t: It's the only one I've got!

cap01_k06.t: Behind them, the ink follows along the wall, the ceiling, the floor, not caring which way gravity points. Nobody explained the rules to it, so it has none.

cap01_k07.t: (Even the monster has more freedom than me.)

cap01_k08.t: At the end of the corridor, a circular hatch starts to close with a slow, hydraulic, bureaucratic noise.

cap01_k12.t: Jair runs along the ceiling. Jumps. Gravity flips mid-jump and pulls him down, toward the real floor, just in time to roll under the hatch.

cap01_k13.t: The hatch closes behind them. On the other side, something hits the metal. Once. Twice. Then, silence.

cap01_k15.t: It went to find another way. They always find another way.

cap01_k17.t: I don't know what a debt collector is, but it sounds horrible.

cap01_g3_035.t: They reach a stone bridge between two floating towers. A chunk is missing from the middle. The gap is about three meters. Below, the void.

cap01_g3_039.t: With this gravity you jump twice as far.

cap01_g3_040.t: With normal gravity I can't jump half that.

cap01_g3_041.t: Behind them, the ink climbs the bridge. The stones darken where it touches them, like photos burning from the corner.

cap01_g3_044.t: It's the first time I've said your name. Don't make me use it at your funeral.

cap01_g3_045a.t: Jair runs. Three steps. Four. The edge.

cap01_g3_045b.t: Jair closes his eyes and runs. If he can't see the void, the void doesn't exist. It's the same technique he uses with his bank statement.

cap01_g3_046.t: For an endless second, they both float over the stars. The magenta sky above, below, everywhere. Cami has her arms around his neck. He doesn't remember when she did that.

cap01_g3_047.t: And they land. Badly. Jair falls to his knees, Cami falls on top of him, and Jair's glasses go flying and stay floating in the air, spinning, two meters from the edge.

cap01_g3_050.t: Without my glasses I can't see the monster!

cap01_g3_052.t: Jair stretches out his arm. The glasses float. His fingers brush them. He catches them.

cap01_g3_053.t: He puts them on just in time to see the monster reach the other side of the bridge, stop at the edge of the gap and... not jump.

cap01_g3_054.t: It stays there, rippling, turning its hole toward them. Like a dog behind a fence.

cap01_g3_056.t: I don't know. They never jump. They never cross gaps.

cap01_g3_057.t: (Navigation limit. It doesn't know how to cross gaps. It's a bug.)

cap01_g3_059.t: (Bugs have saved me more than any person in my life.)

cap01_g3_059g.t: (If this were on Geekdump, someone would have already opened an issue: «monster doesn't cross gaps». With three thumbs up. And nobody would fix it for years.)

cap01_g3_060.t: Navigation error in hostile entity. Patch scheduled.

cap01_g3_063.t: ...Great. Fantastic. That's the level of detail I give my customers.

cap01_g3_068.t: The monster melts into the floor and disappears into the cracks. It didn't leave: it just stopped being visible. Jair knows the difference well. It's the same as between paying off a debt and not opening the mail.

cap01_g3_069.t: There. That hatch. There's a shelter. Take me.

cap01_g3_071.t: Take me, please, or I'll bite you.

cap01_g4_001.t: The shelter is a round capsule of white metal, embedded in the wall of the tower. Inside there are two seats, a dead control panel and an emergency light that blinks halfheartedly.

cap01_g4_002.t: Jair sets Cami down in one of the seats. She grits her teeth and says nothing. It's the closest she's come to thanking him.

cap01_g4_005.t: I took a first aid course.

cap01_g4_007.t: Well, I started it. Online. It was mandatory at work. I got up to module three.

cap01_g4_008.t: And what was in module three?

cap01_g4_010.t: Cami looks at him with a mix of contempt and resignation. Then she stretches out her leg and rests it on the seat across from her.

cap01_g4_011.t: If it hurts, I'll hit you.

cap01_g4_012.t: If it hurts, it means it's working.

cap01_g4_014.t: My supervisor says it about work.

cap01_g4_015.t: Jair finds a first aid kit under the panel. Inside there are bandages, a spray that smells of mint and electricity, and a manual written in a language that looks like English if you squint.

cap01_g4_016.t: He bandages her ankle as best he can. It doesn't look pretty. It looks like the code he writes on a Friday at four in the afternoon: it works, but nobody should see it.

cap01_g4_020.t: (That's also the story of my life.)

cap01_g4_021.t: They fall silent. Through the round porthole, the castle ruins slowly turn against the magenta sky. It's beautiful in a way that makes no sense. Like a screensaver somebody made with love.

cap01_g4_023.t: Exactly? In the ruins of the Bastion. In the space dimension.

cap01_g4_025.t: What corner did you crawl out of that you don't know that?

cap01_g4_026.t: A very small one. With wifi.

cap01_g4_027.t: There are several. This is the space one: stars, fleets, stations, everything that flies. It's mine.

cap01_g4_028.t: And there's the ancestral one. Everything there is old. Kingdoms, castles with roofs, trees hundreds of years old. People who talk funny and bow to say hello.

cap01_g4_029.t: And how do you get there?

cap01_g4_030.t: Through the Rift. It's a portal in the core of the Bastion. The last one still open.

cap01_g4_031.t: And why would anyone want to go to the ancestral dimension?

cap01_g4_032.t: Because here the Evil King already won.

cap01_g4_033.t: She says it without drama. Like someone reporting the weather. Like someone announcing that payday is pushed to next Friday.

cap01_g4_037.t: Nobody's seen him. Only the Federation, which works for him now: his soldiers in black, his monsters. They say that before he was king of everything he was king of something else. A small kingdom. Of flowers.

cap01_g4_038.t: (I asked the AI for an Evil King and it gave him a past. I don't even have a past that elaborate.)

cap01_g4_039.t: And you? What were you doing here alone?

cap01_g4_040.t: Cami takes a while to answer. She looks out the porthole.

cap01_g4_041.t: I wasn't alone. There were more of us. A whole Resistance fleet.

cap01_g4_045.t: I remember the fleet. I remember the noise of the engines. I remember there was a captain who yelled a lot.

cap01_g4_045b.t: I remember my planet joined the Federation through a war. That my parents didn't make it out of that war. That I do know. I know it the way you know a date.

cap01_g4_046.t: But I don't remember their faces. Or their names. Or how I got here. It's like...

cap01_g4_047.t: She makes a gesture with her hand, as if catching something in the air, and when she opens it there's nothing there.

cap01_g4_048.t: It's as if someone told me my life, but never let me live it.

cap01_g4_049.t: Jair says nothing. He feels a cold that has nothing to do with space.

cap01_g4_050.t: Entity 01: background memory generated. Coherence: partial.

cap01_g4_051.t: (Background memory. They gave her filler memories. Like those background characters who say «good morning, traveler» and don't know why.)

cap01_g4_052.t: (And she feels it. She feels they're filler.)
c: Tell her maybe her memories aren't hers

cap01_g4_053a.t: What if those memories aren't yours? What if someone put them there?

cap01_g4_053a3.t: No. Someone... less evil. But just as irresponsible.

cap01_g4_053a4.t: Cami stares at him. Hard. For a moment, Jair thinks she's going to understand. That she's going to ask the right question.

cap01_g4_053a6.t: ...But I'm not going to tell you you're wrong.

cap01_g4_053b.t: Hey. I don't remember half my life either. It's normal.

cap01_g4_053b2.t: Oh, really? What don't you remember?

cap01_g4_053b3.t: Why I studied engineering. Why I'm still at my job. Why I've spent eight years in something that has no name.

cap01_g4_053b4.t: That's not forgetting. That's not wanting to know.

cap01_g4_053c.t: And the gun? Does it have a name?

cap01_g4_053c4.t: It's a gun. Its name is gun.

cap01_g4_053c5.t: But she stares at it for a second, the gun, as if it had never occurred to her that it could be called something else.

cap01_g4_054.t: Your turn. What are you? And don't tell me «tech support».

cap01_g4_057.t: Someone who tells machines what to do.

cap01_g4_060.t: And do they pay you well?

cap01_g4_061.t: They owe me half a month.

cap01_g4_062.t: Cami laughs. It's the first time. A short, dry laugh, with the edge of a knife.

cap01_g4_063.t: Wait. You give orders to machines, they don't pay you... and you say all of this is your dream.

cap01_g4_064.t: How sweet: a god who dreams about his overdue paycheck.

cap01_g4_065.t: You give orders to machines and they still don't pay you. What a sad trade.

cap01_g4_067.t: And do you have someone? Back there, in your corner with wifi?

cap01_g4_068.t: The question catches him off guard. He thinks of Nikki getting into the taxi. That she didn't say goodbye. That he doesn't know if she got home.

cap01_g4_072.t: Nothing's complicated. People say «it's complicated» when the answer is «no».

cap01_g4_075.t: Not even I know I'm here.

cap01_g4_076.t: Then you don't owe her any explanations.

cap01_g4_077.t: She says it looking out the porthole, casually. But the «she» came out with an edge it didn't have before.

cap01_g4_078.t: (Is she jealous? She can't be jealous. I met her twenty minutes ago.)

cap01_g4_079.t: (Well. I met her twenty minutes ago and designed her three hours ago. I don't know how you count that.)

cap01_b01.t: Hey. Before we go on, take this.

cap01_b02.t: She pulls a second, smaller pistol from her belt and offers it to him grip first.

cap01_b04.t: So you stop being dead weight. With a broken ankle I can't cover both of us.

cap01_b06.t: Nothing? Not even in your corner with wifi?

cap01_b07.t: Once I fired a stapler by accident. I hit the head of HR.

cap01_b09.t: They sent me to a workplace harmony course.

cap01_b10.t: Well. This is similar, but without the course.

cap01_b11.t: Jair takes the pistol. It's light and cold, with a blue glow in the barrel that pulses like a tiny heart.

cap01_b12.t: You aim. You breathe. You squeeze. Don't close your eyes.

cap01_b13.t: And if I close my eyes?

cap01_b14.t: Then you hit what you don't want to hit. Like everything in life.

cap01_b15.t: Jair aims at an empty can floating next to the porthole. Breathes. Squeezes.

cap01_b17.t: He squeezes again. Nothing. A little red light turns on in the grip.

cap01_b18.t: User not authorized to carry weapons. Role assigned: companion.

cap01_b21.t: It won't let me shoot. It says I'm... a companion.

cap01_b26.t: Cami takes the pistol from him, aims at the can without looking and fires. The can vanishes in a blue flash.

cap01_b27.t: Works perfectly. The problem is you.

cap01_b28.t: (In my own world they won't even let me be the hero. I got stuck as the companion.)

cap01_b29.t: (Well. At least here they don't dock it from my salary.)

cap01_b30.t: Then you carry and I shoot. It's a good division of labor.

cap01_b31.t: It's the best division of labor I've ever had in my life.

cap01_g4_080.t: The emergency light stops blinking. It stays on. Red.

cap01_g4_083.t: That someone set off the Bastion alarm. That more soldiers are coming.

cap01_g5h_001.t: They leave the shelter. This time Jair carries Cami on his back, like a very angry backpack.

cap01_g5h_005.t: The corridors of the Bastion are wide and tall, with white stone columns mixed with pipes and light panels. As if someone had built a cathedral and then installed cables in it.

cap01_g5h_006.t: (Fantasy with science fiction. That's what I asked for. Literally that.)

cap01_g5h_007.t: The core is down below. Seven levels. We have to go down the central shaft.

cap01_g5h_010.t: I have to work on Monday.

cap01_c01.t: Around a bend in the corridor there's a vending machine. A real one: glass, metal spirals, numbered buttons. Inside there are colorful packets with names Jair doesn't recognize and a single can that says «WATER».

cap01_c02.t: (A vending machine in a space fortress. I asked for fantasy with science fiction and the AI understood «office with stars».)

cap01_c05.t: You look like you have money. Pay.

cap01_c06.t: Look like I have money? Nobody's ever told me that.

cap01_c07.t: You look like you have money saved up and never spend it. Which is similar.

cap01_c08.t: (Nikki told me exactly the same thing a few hours ago. How many women are going to read my savings account today?)

cap01_c09.t: Jair takes out his bank card. The machine has no card slot. It has a star-shaped coin slot.

cap01_c10.t: He takes out his two coins. Neither is star-shaped. He tries to push one in anyway.

cap01_c11.t: Coin not recognized. The user's currency is not valid in this dimension.

cap01_c12.t: Years of saving. Not valid in this dimension.

cap01_c14.t: That I'm broke in every universe.

cap01_c15.t: Cami looks at him. Then at the machine. Then she smashes the glass with the butt of her pistol.

cap01_c16.t: The glass breaks. The can of water falls.

cap01_c19.t: From whom? The machine? The machine belongs to the Evil King.

cap01_c20.t: (Technically, if this is my dream, the machine is mine. I'm stealing from myself.)

cap01_c21.t: (It's the most responsible thing I've done with my money in years.)

cap01_c22.t: He picks up the can. Opens it. They take turns drinking. The water tastes like water, but real water, cold, perfect, and for a second it's the best thing Jair has ever tasted.

cap01_c23.t: See? Sometimes breaking the glass is the right thing.

cap01_c24.t: (Something tells me that line is going to come back to haunt me.)

cap01_g5h_013.t: On level two, the corridor opens into a huge hangar.

cap01_g5h_014.t: There are ships. Dozens. Small fighters with blade-shaped wings, round transports like beetles and, in the center, a big ship with its hull open like a tuna can.

cap01_g5h_015.t: They're all powered down. All covered in a fine silver dust that sparkles when the light hits it.

cap01_g5h_018.t: These are the ships from your fleet?

cap01_g5h_019.t: I think so. I remember that one. The big one. I remember it had a drawing on the door.

cap01_g5h_020.t: Jair walks up to the big ship. There's no drawing on the door. There's a smooth gray rectangle, the size of a window, with small letters in one corner.

cap01_g5h_023.t: Do you see the drawing? It was a... it was a...

cap01_g5h_024.t: Cami frowns. She searches for the word. She can't find it. She searches for the image. She can't find it.
c: Lie to her: «Yes, it's really pretty»

cap01_g5h_025a3.t: There's a gray rectangle. Nothing else.

cap01_g5h_025a4.t: Cami looks at the door for a long time. Jair feels her tense up on his back, feels her stop breathing for a moment.

cap01_g5h_025a5.t: There was one. I saw it.

cap01_g5h_025a7.t: (I don't know what to tell her. There's no module for this.)

cap01_g5h_025b.t: Yes. I see it. It's really pretty.

cap01_g5h_025b3.t: Cami smiles. A tiny smile, of relief. Jair feels he just did something kind and something terrible at the same time, and he can't tell one from the other.

cap01_g5h_025b4.t: (I'm doing to her what Nikki does to me: telling her what she wants to hear so she stays calm.)

cap01_g5h_026.t: If we could start a ship, we wouldn't need the Rift. We could fly anywhere.

cap01_g5h_027.t: Do you know how to start them?

cap01_g5h_028.t: Of course I do. I'm a pilot. Put me down next to that fighter.

cap01_g5h_029.t: Jair sets her down next to a small silver fighter. Cami climbs into the cockpit, presses buttons, pulls levers, punches the dashboard.

cap01_g5h_031.t: I don't get it. It should work.

cap01_g5h_033.t: You? What are you going to try?

cap01_g5h_035.t: Jair looks under the dashboard. He finds a thick cable connected to a round socket. He unplugs it. Counts to ten. Plugs it back in.

cap01_g5h_036.t: The dashboard lights up. Green lights, blue lights, a cheerful beep.

cap01_g5h_039.t: I turned it off and on again.

cap01_g5h_041.t: That's ninety percent of my career.

cap01_g5h_042.t: The dashboard lights flicker. A message appears on the central screen: «ENGINE NOT FOUND».

cap01_g5h_044.t: «Engine not found»? What do you mean not found? It's right back there! I can see it!

cap01_g5h_045.t: Jair looks back. There's something shaped like an engine. It's the size of an engine and the color of an engine. But when he touches it, his hand goes through the surface as if it were smoke.

cap01_g5h_046.t: (It's set dressing. The ships are set dressing. They were never made to fly.)

cap01_g5h_049.t: Jair? What's wrong? Why are you making that face?

cap01_g5h_050.t: It doesn't work. We have to go to the Rift.

cap01_g5h_053.t: She doesn't insist. She climbs out of the cockpit slowly, leaning on him, and looks at the whole hangar one last time: the dozens of sleeping ships, the silver dust, the fleet that maybe never existed.

cap01_g5m_001.t: As they leave the hangar, something vibrates in Jair's pocket.

cap01_g5m_003.t: Twelve percent battery. And one bar. A single bar of signal, blinking, impossible.

cap01_g5m_005.t: A notification. A message from Nikki, sent at 2:41 a.m.

cap01_g5m_009.t: Jair stares at the screen. Three messages with no capitals or punctuation, typed with one eye closed from the back seat of a taxi.

cap01_g5m_010.t: (She got home. She got home safe.)

cap01_g5m_011h1.t: At the top, Nikki's picture has a colored ring. She posted a story.

cap01_g5m_011h2.t: Jair opens it. Nikki at The Last One, beer in hand and cheeks red, smiling at the phone. On top, in white letters: «just one».

cap01_g5m_011h5.t: The story lasts five seconds. Jair watches it three times.

cap01_g5m_011h6.t: Then he goes back to the chat.

cap01_g5m_012.t: He feels something in his chest he can't name. It's the closest thing to being home he's felt since he woke up under the magenta sky.

cap01_g5m_014.t: A phone. It's... a device for talking to people who are far away.

c: Tell her the truth: «A friend. Nikki»

cap01_g5m_016a5.t: That she got home. Not to be mad. Good morning.

cap01_g5m_016a6.t: I don't know what time it is here. But it's not morning.

cap01_g5m_016a9.t: Cami doesn't say anything else. But for the next ten minutes, every time Jair takes a step, she squeezes his shoulder a little harder than necessary.

cap01_g5m_016b4.t: Messages you didn't ask for, from people you don't care about.

cap01_g5m_016b7.t: You're the worst liar in two dimensions.

cap01_g5m_017.t: Jair tries to reply. He types «home ok?», as if he didn't already know. He hits send.

cap01_g5m_018.t: The signal bar disappears. The message stays with a little clock next to it. Waiting.

cap01_g5m_019.t: External connection detected and closed. It is recommended not to repeat.

cap01_g5m_020.t: («It is recommended»? Since when does a program recommend things?)

cap01_g5m_021.t: He puts the phone away. Eleven percent.

cap01_g5_001.t: They go down a spiral staircase that winds around a shaft of blue light. Jair counts the steps because counting gives him something to do with the fear. One hundred twelve. One hundred thirteen.

cap01_g5_002.t: On level four, Cami covers his mouth with her hand.

cap01_g5_004.t: Below, in the corridor, five masked soldiers walk in single file. Black armor. Identical steps. Heads turning left, right, left, all at once, like a single neck shared by five bodies.

cap01_g5_005.t: (Whispering) There are too many. With this ankle I can't take three.

cap01_g5_006.t: (Whispering) What if we wait for them to leave?

cap01_g5_007.t: (Whispering) They don't leave. They patrol. Round and round. They never get tired.

cap01_g5_009.t: Jair watches. Really watches, the way he watches an error log when everyone else has given up.

cap01_g5_010.t: The soldiers walk to the column at the back. Turn. Walk to the door. Turn. Stop for four seconds in front of a light panel. Walk again.

cap01_g5_011.t: To the column. Turn. To the door. Turn. Four seconds in front of the panel.

cap01_g5_012.t: To the column. Turn. To the door. Turn. Four seconds.

cap01_g5_014.t: (It's a perfect loop. It never changes. It never improvises.)

cap01_g5_015.t: (Just like me. Office, bus, home. Office, bus, home. Four seconds in front of the open fridge.)

cap01_g5_016.t: (I know exactly how to outsmart someone like that. I've been someone like that my whole life.)

cap01_g5_017.t: (Whispering) When they reach the column, we have eight seconds to cross without being seen. When they stop in front of the panel, another four.

cap01_g5_019.t: (Whispering) Because I've been living in that loop for thirty years.

c: Cross now, before your legs start shaking

cap01_g5_023c.t: (Eight seconds. Too many soldiers. The math doesn't work. But the math never worked for me and here I am.)

cap01_g5_023c2.t: Jair steps out from behind the column, plants himself in front of the nearest soldier and raises his fists like in the movies. Like in the movies he watched as a kid, from the couch.

cap01_g5_023c3.t: The soldier looks at him, or does something like looking with a faceless helmet. Then pushes him with one hand. No force. No interest. Like someone moving a chair out of the way.

cap01_g5_023c4.t: Jair rolls two meters and ends up behind the column again, sitting, fists still raised.

cap01_g5_023c8.t: (Whispering) They recognized you as furniture. Now do your loop thing and don't improvise again.

cap01_g5_023c9.t: (It's the most honest performance review I've ever had.)

cap01_g5_024a.t: Jair waits. Counts. The soldiers reach the column. Turn.

cap01_g5_024a3.t: He crosses the corridor with Cami on his back, on tiptoe, holding his breath. Eight seconds. Seven. Six.

cap01_g5_024a4.t: They reach the shadow of the staircase on the other side just as the five helmets turn toward where they had been.

cap01_g5_024a5.t: Nothing. The soldiers walk on. Column. Turn. Door. Turn.

cap01_g5_024a7.t: (Whispering) It always works. Nobody checks the loops.

cap01_g5_024a8.t: (Whispering) Coming from you, that sounds really sad.

cap01_g5_024a9.t: (Whispering) Everything sounds really sad coming from me. It's my voice.

cap01_g5_024b.t: Jair doesn't wait. If he waits, he'll think. And if he thinks, he'll never cross.

cap01_g5_024b2.t: He crosses. At the wrong time. The soldiers are mid-turn.

cap01_g5_024b3.t: A helmet stops. Turns toward him. The black hole of the mask looks at him.

cap01_g5_024b4.t: (There it is. The price of not following protocol.)

cap01_g5_024b7.t: Jair runs. Three steps. On the fourth, the corridor ahead fills with helmets. Five more. Ten more. All of them turn their heads at once, toward him.

cap01_g5_024b8.t: Cami fires. A soldier falls. Two. Three. But for every one that falls an identical one appears behind it, as if someone were copying and pasting.

cap01_g5_024b9.t: There are too many! Put me down, I'll stay and cover you!

cap01_g5_024b11.t: It's the bravest thing Jair has ever said. It lasts exactly one second, which is how long it takes for an energy net to fall on both of them.

cap01_g5_024b12.t: The soldiers surround them. The smooth masks look at them without eyes.

cap01_g5_024b13.t: Unregistered entity. Unknown origin. Procedure: archive.

cap01_g5_024b14.t: Archive? What do you mean archive?

cap01_g5_024b16.t: The cell is white, small and windowless. It has a cot, a light that never turns off and, on the other side of the bars, Cami's cell. She doesn't talk to him.

cap01_g5_024b17.t: (Four walls. A light. Nobody to call me.)

cap01_g5_024b18.t: (It's just like my apartment, but without the fan.)

cap01_g5_025.t: They keep going down. Level five. Level six. The blue light of the shaft grows more intense, almost white, and starts to hum.

cap01_g5_030.t: You looked at them like you understood them. Like you knew how they were made.

cap01_g5_032.t: That scares me more than the monster.

cap01_g6_001.t: The core of the Bastion is a circular hall the size of a stadium, its ceiling lost in darkness and the floor covered in cables as thick as tree trunks.

cap01_g6_002.t: In the center, floating a meter off the ground, is the Rift.

cap01_g6_003.t: It isn't a neat round portal, like in the movies. It's a wound. A vertical tear in the air, with jagged edges, leaking golden light and a wind that smells of wet earth and old wood.

cap01_g6_004.t: (It smells like rain. I haven't smelled real rain in months. In my city it only rains heat.)

cap01_g6_007.t: No. They only told me about it.

cap01_g6_009.t: As they get closer, the Rift trembles. It closes a little. It opens a little more. Like an eye trying not to fall asleep.

cap01_g6_010.t: Bridge between dimensions: unstable. Ancestral dimension autocomplete: 68%.

cap01_g6_011.t: Sixty-eight percent? The other side isn't finished yet?

cap01_g6_012.t: It is recommended to wait for 100%.

cap01_g6_015.t: (It's the same answer my company gives about my salary.)

cap01_g6_017.t: They say the Rift is unstable.

cap01_g6_018.t: Your voices are geniuses. Look: it's closing.

cap01_g6_019.t: Jair takes a step toward the Rift.

cap01_g6_020.t: And then the lights come on.

cap01_g6_021.t: All at once. White, harsh, operating-room lights. Soldiers appear on the balconies around the hall. Ten. Twenty. Thirty. All with the same faceless mask. All aiming.

cap01_g6_022.t: And on the catwalk over the Rift, a figure taller than the rest. Dark gray armor, thick worn plates, with copper-colored edges. A closed helmet with a red V-shaped visor that glows like an ember. An assault rifle with a scope, held with the calm of someone who has never had to lower it.

cap01_g6_023.t: Warrior. We thought you were dead.

cap01_g6_024.t: People have thought I was dead lots of times. I'm hard to convince.

cap01_g6_026.t: The red visor turns toward Jair. Jair feels that eyeless gaze on the back of his neck, in his stomach, in his account balance.

cap01_g6_027.t: That one isn't in the records.

cap01_g6_028.t: (Apparently not in my company's payroll records either.)

cap01_g6_029.t: Unregistered entity. Unknown origin. Procedure: eliminate.

cap01_g6_030.t: Wait, wait! I'm a civilian! I have rights! I have a contract!

cap01_g6_032.t: ...That's a question I ask myself too.

cap01_g6_033.t: (Whispering) Jair. Listen to me. When I say so, you run to the Rift. You don't stop. You don't look back.

cap01_g6_035.t: (Whispering) I'm on your back, genius. I go wherever you go.

cap01_g6_039.t: (Whispering) If we die, it was a pleasure meeting the worst hero in the space dimension.

cap01_g6_040.t: (Whispering) Likewise. I mean... thanks. I mean...

cap01_g6_042.t: Cami raises her pistol and fires. Not at the soldiers: at the ceiling. At a bundle of cables hanging over the catwalk.

cap01_g6_043.t: The cables snap in a shower of blue sparks. The operating-room lights flicker, go out and come back at half strength. The hall fills with shadows and flashes.

cap01_g6_045.t: The soldiers' shots whiz around him, red and long, like the lines of a chart in free fall.

cap01_g6_046.t: One passes so close it singes his sleeve. The black printed shirt. The usual one.

cap01_g6_050.t: I'LL BUY YOU ANOTHER ONE! RUN!

cap01_g6_051.t: (She has no money. Nobody here has money. But it's the nicest promise anyone's made me in years.)

cap01_g6_052.t: The captain jumps down from the catwalk. He lands between Jair and the Rift with a thud that shakes the floor, and aims the rifle straight at his face.

cap01_g6_053c.t: (He has a rifle. I have a singed shirt. Seems fair.)

cap01_g6_053c2.t: Jair runs at the captain. Not at the Rift, not at Cami: at the rifle. It's the bravest decision of his life and it lasts a second and a half.

cap01_g6_053c4.t: The red visor lights up. The shot makes no sound: just a red light, very clean, that goes through him at chest height.

cap01_g6_053c5.t: Jair falls to his knees. It doesn't hurt. That's the worst part: nothing hurts, like in dreams.

cap01_g6_053c8.t: (At least this time I didn't run away.)

cap01_g6_053c9.t: (What a bad moment I picked to start.)

cap01_g6_054a.t: Jair does the only thing he's good at: avoiding conflict.

cap01_g6_054a2.t: He ducks, throws himself sideways and rolls across the floor with Cami on top, in a way that has nothing heroic about it and everything of someone slipping in the shower.

cap01_g6_054a3.t: The rifle's red burst passes right where his head was and singes one of his curls.

cap01_g6_054a4.t: That was the clumsiest thing I've ever seen in my life!

cap01_g6_054b2.t: I know I have to shoot him! I don't need a supervisor!

cap01_g6_054b3.t: Cami fires three times over Jair's shoulder. The captain shields himself with his armored forearm and two shots bounce off the plates. The third hits the visor and splits it in half.

cap01_g6_054b4.t: There's no face underneath either. Just the same smooth gray surface. But in the center, for an instant, some white letters flicker.

cap01_g6_054b6.t: (They didn't even give him a name.)

cap01_g6_054b7.t: (He has less identity than I do. And that's saying something.)

cap01_g6_055.t: The Rift is five meters away. Four. It's closing: it's not a door anymore, it's a slit as wide as a person.

cap01_g6_060.t: For an instant, the shots stop. The noise stops. Everything stops.

cap01_g6_061.t: And then the golden light swallows them.

cap01_g6c_002.t: Not downward: in every direction. The world comes apart in strips of color. Magenta, gold, green, a blue that has no name.

cap01_g6c_003.t: They pass fragments of other places: a desert of glass; a frozen forest; a city of curved roofs under a rain of petals; a small room with a spinning fan.

cap01_g6c_005.t: The room goes by before he can be sure. Above the bed, for a fraction of a second, he thought he saw a poster.

cap01_g6c_006.t: Transferring entities: space dimension → ancestral dimension.

cap01_g6c_008.t: Unregistered entity: JAIR. Integrity: not applicable.

cap01_i01.t: Suddenly, ground. A ground that isn't the end: an island of glass floating in nothing, in the middle of the fall.

cap01_i02.t: Jair rolls onto it with Cami. The glass is transparent: below it you can see other strips of color, other falls, other half-made worlds.

cap01_i04.t: I don't think so. This looks like... a waiting room.

cap01_i05.t: The island creaks. A white light rises through the cracks in the glass and, with the light, a hum, like an overheating server.

cap01_i09.t: We're STANDING ON the unassigned fragment!

cap01_i10.t: The glass starts disappearing from the edges. It doesn't break: it gets erased. Like a selection someone drags with the mouse before hitting «delete».

cap01_i13.t: Toward the gold! Always toward the gold!

cap01_i14.t: Jair lifts her, runs the three meters of island that are left and jumps toward the golden strip just as the last piece of glass vanishes under his feet.

cap01_i15.t: (A «delete» almost erased me. Me, who's deleted so many things without thinking twice.)

cap01_g6c_010.t: Cami hugs him tighter. She says nothing. Her eyes are closed and her face is hidden in his neck.

cap01_g6c_011.t: Jair doesn't know if it's fear. He doesn't know if it's the wind. He doesn't know if he has the right to feel what he's feeling for someone who's existed for three hours.

cap01_g6c_013.t: (No. Nikki wouldn't laugh. Nikki would go very quiet and then order another round.)

cap01_g7_002.t: Real grass. Damp, cold, smelling of earth after the rain. Jair ends up on his back, with Cami on top of him, looking at a sky that isn't magenta.

cap01_g7_003.t: It's golden. A still, eternal sunset, the color of old honey.

cap01_g7_005.t: You're alive. I'm on top of you. Those are two different things.

cap01_g7_008.t: She doesn't get off. Two seconds. Three. Then she rolls to one side and lies in the grass, looking at the sky, breathing hard.

cap01_g7_009.t: My ankle. I hit it when we fell.

cap01_g7_011.t: Bad enough that you'll have to carry me again. Don't get excited.

cap01_g7_015.t: Jair sits up and looks around.

cap01_g7_016.t: They're in a clearing, in the middle of a forest. But it's not a normal forest. The trees on the left have pink flowers, like cherry trees. The ones in front have green leaves full of sun. The ones on the right have red and orange leaves that fall slowly. And the ones at the back are bare, covered in snow.

cap01_g7_017.t: (Four seasons. At the same time. In the same forest.)

cap01_g7_018.t: (I didn't ask for this. I asked for «a world with an Evil King». Where did all this come from?)

cap01_g7_019.t: Ancestral dimension: autocomplete 100%. History generated: 847 years.

cap01_g7_021.t: How long have I been asleep?

cap01_g7_023.t: Jair feels a vertigo that has nothing to do with the fall. One hour and twelve minutes. Eight hundred forty-seven years. Someone lived those years. Someone was born, grew up and died in this forest while he snored on a keyboard.

cap01_g7_024.t: (And I complain that my week is long.)

cap01_g7_026.t: The trees. Each group is a different season.

cap01_g7_027.t: Oh, yes. They told me about that too. The ancestral dimension has four ancient families: Summer, Spring, Autumn and Winter. Each one had its kingdom.

cap01_g7_029.t: They say one of the four families had a king who wanted everything. Nobody says which one. It's bad luck to say it.

cap01_g7_030.t: And why is it bad luck?

cap01_g7_031.t: Because every time someone says it, one of his soldiers shows up. Or so they say.

cap01_g7_033.t: I wasn't going to. I'm not an idiot.

cap01_g7_034.t: Jair helps her stand up. She leans her weight on him. He puts his arm around her waist. Neither of them comments on it. They're becoming experts at not commenting on anything.

cap01_g7_035.t: We have to find someone who knows this dimension. I don't have maps. I don't have a fleet. I don't have...

cap01_g7_038.t: He says it without thinking. He regrets it as soon as he finishes saying it. It's the cheesiest line he's ever said, and that's counting the time he told Nikki she was «his favorite variable».

cap01_g7_043.t: And for the first time, Cami doesn't say it mockingly.
c: Offer her your shoulder to walk

cap01_g7_044a.t: Jair crouches and lifts her in his arms, like in the castle. She doesn't protest. She just puts an arm around his neck and looks the other way.

cap01_g7_044b.t: Lean on me. We'll walk slowly.

cap01_g7_044b2.t: They walk slowly. Ten steps. Fifteen. On step sixteen, Cami's ankle gives way and she lets out a word not even autocomplete dares to translate.

cap01_g7_044b3.t: Carry me. And not a word.

cap01_g7_044b5.t: Jair lifts her in his arms.

cap01_g7_045.t: They walk among the trees, crossing from spring to summer and from summer to autumn. The leaves crunch. Petals fall on Cami's blond hair and she doesn't brush them off.

cap01_g7_046.t: For a while there are no monsters. No soldiers. No late paychecks or taxis or fans. Just the forest, the still sunset and the weight of someone who trusts him enough to let herself be carried.

cap01_g7_048.t: (This is exactly what I asked the machine for. «Take care of me. Don't leave.»)

cap01_g7_049.t: (So why do I feel like I cheated?)

cap01_d03.t: The person in your corner. The «sort of» one. What does she do?

cap01_d07.t: It's... cold food. Sweet. Creamy. You eat it when it's hot out and for a few minutes the heat doesn't matter.

cap01_d09.t: And then it's gone and the heat comes back.

cap01_d11.t: Every good thing in my world is a bit of a trap.

cap01_d12.t: And is she good at selling them?

cap01_d13.t: Really good. She smiles twelve hours straight. Her face is trained.

cap01_d14.t: I wouldn't smile twelve hours for anyone.

cap01_d16.t: But I could sell ice cream. I bet I'd sell more than her.

cap01_d18.t: Because nobody would dare not to buy one from me.

cap01_d19.t: (That's completely true, and it scares me.)

cap01_d20.t: They keep walking. Cami goes quiet for a while, playing with a petal between her fingers.

cap01_d21.t: And you? What do you like most about your world?

cap01_d24.t: Jair thinks. He thinks about the office, the bus, the apartment, the fan. The queue of calls on hold. The savings he never touches.

cap01_d26.t: (Why is this so hard for me?)

cap01_d29.t: At three in the morning nobody asks you for anything. The phone doesn't ring. There's no supervisor. Nobody expects you to do anything. It's the only hour of the day that's mine.

cap01_d30.t: That's not something you like. That's something that doesn't hurt you.

cap01_d32.t: It's not the same, you know?

cap01_d33.t: (I know. I've known for years. But nobody had ever said it out loud.)

cap01_d36.t: Someone carrying me. Even if it's a companion without a gun.

cap01_d37.t: She says it so quietly that Jair isn't sure he heard it. When he looks at her, she's looking at the trees, her face red, with the look of someone who'll kill him if he asks.

cap01_d39.t: (I'm a coward, but I'm not an idiot.)
