cap01_g7b_002.t: Behind them, in the clearing where they landed, something falls from the sky. Not with a thud: with a splash. Like a very large drop of ink falling into a glass of water.

cap01_g7b_005.t: The ink rises from the grass, but not alone: it drags earth, roots and stones from the clearing, which stick to its body like scabs. When it finishes standing up it's bigger than before, almost a meter taller than Jair, covered in rock plates. Between the cracks, the spinning hole.

cap01_g7b_006.t: Patch applied: cross-dimension navigation enabled for hostile entities.

cap01_g7b_009.t: (I wish my company answered that fast. I wish it answered at all.)

cap01_g7b_012.t: Jair runs with Cami in his arms, from spring into summer. The monster follows them, and wherever it passes the flowers wither, the grass turns gray and the colors drain out of things, as if someone were erasing the drawing.

cap01_g7b_013.t: Cami fires backward. The blue flashes bounce off the rock and get lost among the trees.

cap01_g7b_014.t: It's useless. It's useless. Nothing works!

cap01_g7b_015.t: Think of something! You're the warrior!

cap01_g7b_016.t: You're the one who understands everything! Understand this!

cap01_g7b_017.t: (Understand this. Understand this. What is it that it can't do?)

cap01_g7b_018.t: (It couldn't cross gaps, and they already patched that. What else? What else didn't they program into it?)

cap01_g7b_019.t: They enter autumn. The red leaves crunch underfoot. Further ahead the forest turns white: winter, with its snow, its silence and a frozen stream running across it from side to side.

cap01_g7b_021.t: (It comes from the space dimension. There's no snow there. No water. No ice.)

cap01_g7b_022.t: (Nobody taught it what to do with ice.)

cap01_g7b_022c.t: (I've run enough. I've run my whole life. Once. Just once I want to stay.)

cap01_g7b_022c2.t: Jair sets Cami down in the snow, behind a rock, and turns around.

cap01_g7b_022c3.t: What are you doing? Jair! The ice! The ice thing!

cap01_g7b_022c4.t: The armored monster comes out of autumn. The rocks covering its body crack in the cold. Every step leaves a hole in the snow.

cap01_g7b_022c5.t: Hey! This is my dream! I'm in charge here!

cap01_g7b_022c7.t: The monster doesn't slow down. It doesn't even seem to notice Jair is there until it's on top of him.

cap01_g7b_022c8.t: The last thing Jair sees is the white winter sky, and Cami shouting something at him he can't quite hear, like the Voice when it speaks very softly.

cap01_g7b_022c9.t: (The ice. She was right about the ice.)

cap01_g7b_023a.t: Jair leaves the path and throws himself onto the frozen stream. The ice creaks. He slips. He falls on his back, shielding Cami with his body, and slides across the surface like a penguin with glasses.

cap01_g7b_023a2.t: Behind them, the monster reaches the bank. It stretches a tip of ink over the ice.

cap01_g7b_023a4.t: First the tip. Then the arm, or whatever that is. Then the rest, in a wave of frost that climbs and climbs until the whole monster is still, transparent, trapped in a statue of black ice and stone.

cap01_g7b_023a6.t: It didn't know what ice was. It never saw it. They didn't write rules for that.

cap01_g7b_023a8.t: I didn't. I guessed. That's how I do almost everything.

cap01_g7b_023b.t: Jair dives behind a fallen trunk, onto a snowbank, and covers them both with loose snow. Cold. Very cold. It gets into his shirt collar.

cap01_g7b_023b2.t: (Whispering) This is your plan? Bury us?

cap01_g7b_023b3.t: (Whispering) It's the plan I've used with my problems for years.

cap01_g7b_023b4.t: The monster enters winter. It moves over the snow. And wherever the snow touches it, the ink turns stiff, slow, dull.

cap01_g7b_023b5.t: It takes three more steps. Two. One. And it stops, still, transparent, turned into a statue of black ice and stone half a meter from the trunk.

cap01_g7b_023b7.t: (Whispering) It didn't know what snow was. It had never seen it.

cap01_g7b_023b8.t: (Whispering) Neither have you, judging by your face.

cap01_g7b_023b9.t: (Whispering) It doesn't snow in my city. It's just hot. All year.

cap01_g7b_024.t: They stare at the black ice statue for a long while. Inside, the hole it has for a face keeps spinning, very slowly, like a clock that doesn't know it has stopped.

cap01_g7b_027.t: Don't make me say it again.

cap01_g7b_028.t: No, seriously, I didn't hear you. The wind.

cap01_g7b_029.t: I said thanks, idiot. You saved me. Twice. Three times, counting the bridge.

cap01_g7b_030.t: You saved me too. With the soldiers.

cap01_g7b_035.t: Cami laughs. This time the laugh has no edge. It's short, tired and honest, and it slips out without permission.

cap01_g8_001.t: At the edge of winter there's a stone path, and over the path, a red wooden bridge crossing a stream.

cap01_g8_002.t: And in the middle of the bridge, with her back to them, there's someone.

cap01_g8_003.t: A woman in a red kimono. Long green hair, so green it looks hand-painted. A blue flower tucked behind her ear.

cap01_g8_004.t: She's standing still, looking at the water. At her waist she carries a sword: a black hilt with no blade, as if the blade were something you only draw when it's needed.

cap01_g8_006.t: (The green-haired one in the red kimono.)

cap01_g8_007.t: Cami tenses in his arms. She lowers her hand to her pistol.

cap01_g8_010.t: (Whispering) No. That's why you don't move.

cap01_g8_011.t: The woman in the kimono speaks without turning around.

cap01_g8_012.t: I've been on this bridge a long time.

cap01_g8_013.t: I've seen whole winters go by. I've seen kingdoms fall. I've seen people I loved leave down different roads.

cap01_g8_014.t: And in all that time, nobody ever came to this forest from above. Nobody fell from the sky.

cap01_g8_016.t: She has the eyes of someone who has waited a long time. Too long. And who isn't sure what she was waiting for was worth it.

cap01_g8_018.t: Her eyes go from Jair to Cami. From Cami to Jair. And they stop on Jair's arms, on the way he holds Cami, on the way Cami has an arm around his neck.

cap01_g8_019.t: Something twists in her face. Very fast. Almost nothing. Like a cloud covering the sun for a second.

cap01_g8_020.t: And who are you two? And why is she... like that? On top of you?

cap01_g8_021.t: I'm not on top. I'm being transported.

cap01_g8_022.t: Very comfortably, from what I can see.

cap01_g8_023.t: Do you have a problem with that?

cap01_g8_024.t: I don't have any problems. I never have problems. Problems have me.

cap01_g8_025.t: (What's going on? Why is there tension? We just got here. We don't even know her name.)

cap01_g8_028.t: (I deleted it. I deleted it myself. I'm sure I deleted it.)

cap01_g8_031a.t: Sorry. Hi. My name's Jair. This is Cami. We come from... up there. Literally. We don't want any trouble.

cap01_g8_031a2.t: The woman looks at him. Then she does something Jair didn't expect: she bows. A short, precise, ancient bow.

cap01_g8_031a3.t: At least one of you has manners.

cap01_g8_031a4.t: I have manners. I use them on people who earn them.

cap01_g8_031b.t: No, no, it's not what it looks like. She's just a teammate. She hurt her ankle. It's pure logistics.

cap01_g8_031b4.t: The woman in the kimono relaxes her shoulders. A little. Almost nothing.

cap01_g8_031b6.t: She says it very quietly, just for him. And she digs her nails into his shoulder, very slowly, very deliberately.

cap01_g8_031c.t: We need help. She's hurt, we don't know this place and a faceless army is chasing us. Please.

cap01_g8_031c3.t: I know them. I've been cutting their heads off for centuries. They always come back.

cap01_g8_032.t: I suppose I should introduce myself.

cap01_g8_033.t: She puts her hand on the bladeless hilt. A thin red energy blade springs from it, humming like a violin string.

cap01_g8_034.t: She spins the sword: elegant, unnecessary, completely theatrical. A few petals falling nearby are split in two in midair.

cap01_g8_036.t: Entity 02: RIKKA. Name assigned by autocomplete.

cap01_g8_037.t: Guardian of this bridge. Last of... well. Last of many things.

cap01_g8_038.t: And if you bring trouble to my forest, I swear on my sisters that...

cap01_g8_039.t: She stops. Frowns. Lowers the sword a little.

cap01_g8_040.t: ...Wait. Are you going to charge me for something?

cap01_g8_042.t: Travelers always charge. For news, for maps, for favors. I don't have money. I never have money. How much does it cost for you to tell me where you're from? I'm scared to ask.

cap01_g8_044.t: It's free. I swear. I never charge. Literally nobody pays me.

cap01_g8_046.t: They owe him half a month.

cap01_g8_047.t: Rikka looks at Jair with a mix of pity and something else. Something like recognizing someone of her own species.

cap01_g8_052.t: Rikka turns off the sword and comes closer. She looks at Cami's ankle: the horrible bandage, the badly tied knot.

cap01_g8_056.t: I got up to module three.

cap01_g8_057.t: I don't know what that means and I don't want to know.

cap01_g8_058.t: Cami and Rikka look at each other up close for the first time. Cami goes still. Something in the green-haired woman's face bothers her: not the face itself, but the feeling of having seen it before. Somewhere else. From behind. As if she had always been one step behind her.

cap01_g8_059.t: (Why do I feel like I already know that back?)

cap01_g8_060.t: On the other side of the bridge there's a shelter. I can heal her ankle. I can give you food. I can tell you which way not to go.

cap01_g8_062.t: She looks at Jair's arms again. At Cami, nicely settled in them.

cap01_g8_065.t: Then hop on one foot. Very comfortably.

cap01_g8_067.t: I don't fight the wounded. I wait for them to heal and then I humiliate them.

cap01_j01.t: Hey. Can we fight later? She's heavy.

cap01_j03.t: That you weigh... very little. You weigh almost nothing. But my arms are office arms.

cap01_j05.t: An office is a place where people sit all day and get sad.

cap01_j10.t: I'm repeating it because it's true.

cap01_j11.t: Rikka sighs, a long theatrical sigh that seems rehearsed over centuries. Then she turns around, her kimono swirling around her like in a painting.

cap01_j12.t: Follow me. And you, the one with the burnt shirt...

cap01_j14.t: Jair. Jair what? Jair the Fallen from the Sky? Jair the Badly Bandaged?

cap01_j18.t: I asked him the same thing. He says it's a very humble order.

cap01_j19.t: It's the first time Cami and Rikka say something in the same tone. They both notice at the same time, and they both make exactly the same disgusted face.

cap01_j20.t: (Rivals. Tension. Jealousy. And, apparently, the same sense of humor.)

cap01_g8_068.t: (Two hours. I've been in this world for two hours and I'm already in the middle of something I don't know the name of.)

cap01_g8_070.t: Behind them, the sun of the eternal sunset doesn't move. Ahead are the red bridge, the shelter and the forest of the four seasons.

cap01_g8_071.t: And in the back of his head, the voice again, so soft that this time Jair can't make it out before it fades.

cap01_g8_072.t: Entities 01 and 02: in contact. Rivalry: active. Autocomplete: continuing.
